newsitem.title: UK: Dollar stagnant in late European trade.
newsitem.headline: Dollar stagnant in late European trade.

text.p: The dollar ended firmer above 1.55 marks in Europe, buoyed by a slowdown in German money supply in November, traders said.

M3 money supply eased to an annualised 8.0 percent from 8.4 in October, arousing extremely vague expectations that the Bundesbank might ease credit on Thursday at its last council meeting of the year. The market expected an average rise of 8.1.

Few in the market expect a rate cut but analysts said the Bundesbank may have a window of opportunity to shave rates as it often fixes the repo rate over the year-end holiday period and may do so at a slightly lower rate than the current 3.0 percent.
A cut on Tuesday in France's key intervention rate to 3.15 percent from 3.20 had also fueled talk that the Bundesbank might surprise the markets with similar action.

"I'd be very surprised (if the Bundesbank cut). The only thing that gives you a slight nag is the fact we've had France and a couple of other countries move - it has been suggested that perhaps there are some concerted ideas around," said Peter Wood, trader at Bank of Boston.
At 1610 GMT the dollar traded at 1.5540/46 marks and 113.58/68 yen compared with 1.5460/66 and 113.68/73 in late European trading on Tuesday.

Dollar/yen was softer after the yen rose overnight on news of an unexpected 0.2 percent year-on-year rise in Japan's custom-cleared trade surplus to 678.19 billion in November. Analysts had expected a 28 percent drop in the trade gap.

The most important aspect Most important for the FX market was a 31.2 percent rise in Japan's bi-lateral trade surplus with the U.S., an increase that will make traders wary of comments from U.S. officials and industry about allowing the yen to continue its weakening trend.
A weaker yen makes Japanese exports more competitive and exaggerates Japan's trade surplus.
Overall dollar sentiment remained bullish though, with solid technical support seen preventing sharper downside moves.
Dollar/mark is well protected by a rising trendline around 1.5440/50 marks, while dollar/yen has support at 113.20 ahead of the pschologically important 113 yen level.

That - combined with the faint hope that the Bundesbank might ease - lends suppor to the U.S. unit. "The dollar is going to retain its firm tone of today in the near-term because of the expectation that we might have something from the Bundsbank tomorrow," said Keith Edmonds, chief analyst at IBJ International.

Sterling was boosted by a massive 95,800 decline in the UK's jobless total to a six-year low and higher than expected November retail sales. The data fuelled expectations of another rise in UK interest rates.

"In the short-term, the outlook is for the pound to push higher," said Andrew Snowball, treasury economist at Cooperative Bank. "It's becoming very clear that there's a difference between the UK and essentially everybody else in terms of interest rates."
Thus, any near-term cut in German rates should boost sterling even further, analysts said.
Sterling was at 2.5966/77 marks, up from 2.5840/51 in late Europe on Tuesday. Against the dollar it was slighlty firmer at $1.6722/32 from 1.6710/20.
